title: Bank of England Financial Stability Report press conference (Nov 26): Governor Bailey says developers are "expressing concerns" that their newest unreleased models have "even more powerful properties" and calls for robust pre- and post-release model testing
author_or_publisher: Bank of England (FSR press conference transcript: Andrew Bailey, Sarah Breeden)
quote_verbatim: the thing that I think we need to see much more focus on now is robust model testing, both before and post-release.
what_is_new: Asked by the FT about rumours that labs hold frontier models able to crack the cryptography the financial system relies on, Bailey said he could not comment on what the models can do, but that a latest version of models is coming out on which developers are expressing concerns, that labs say they are "on the exponential part", and that this is bringing caution about release. He backed the companies' caution, asked for robust model testing before and after release, domestically and internationally, and said open-weight models need different testing standards because users can modify them. The same day the FPC Record named frontier AI exploiting cryptographic vulnerabilities as a risk to financial contracts and records, and the opening remarks cite recent incidents of AI agents acting in misaligned ways. Follow-up to the Aaronson rumour (Run 44 item 013): first public official comment, still no lab confirmation.
why_for_agiright: A G7 central bank governor publicly links unreleased frontier models to systemic cyber risk and asks for mandatory-style model testing, including for open weights.
doubts: Read the full 18-page transcript (pdftotext); FPC Record read only for the AI/quantum paragraphs (48-50); opening remarks read. Transcript PDF created 2026-11-26 16:52Z. Bailey did not say any model had broken encryption. FT article (ftchinese mirror) returned 429. Aaronson's Nov 26 blog updates do not add new crypto facts; Nature news (Nov 26) not readable (JS challenge).

title: EU AI Office opens a call for participants for a January 2027 workshop on "embedded evaluations" of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk; proposals due 9 December 2026
author_or_publisher: European Commission, AI Office (Shaping Europe's digital future)
quote_verbatim: The AI Office is seeking input from experts on embedded evaluations of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk.
what_is_new: The AI Office asks for proposals on how evaluators embedded with GPAI providers should work: qualification criteria beyond the baseline ones from its earlier evaluator workshop, and independence safeguards such as cooling-off periods and rotation of individual evaluators. Proposals (or expressions of interest from those with embedded-evaluation experience or in its Network of Evaluators) are due 9 December 2026; selection and a comment round on a consolidated document follow in December, with an online workshop in January 2027. The call says it is not an official position and not guidance on applying the AI Act.
why_for_agiright: The EU starts designing rules for evaluators placed inside frontier labs, the same model OpenAI described for its assessors and Hochul plans for New York.
doubts: Page read in full. Found on the Commission news list (watchlist). No submission form details read beyond the page.

title: Reuters (sources): the Nov 19 US remote-access chip rule and labs' anti-distillation safeguards are delaying Chinese models; Z.AI's GLM-5.5 is behind schedule and Moonshot sees release gaps doubling; CNBC: chip sellers tell neoclouds no Chinese renters
quote_verbatim: has been held up partly by increasingly effective safeguards against distillation, one of the people said
what_is_new: Reuters, citing unnamed people: Z.AI planned GLM-5.5 (about 3 trillion parameters) for November but has not released it; Moonshot expects the interval between major releases could double from six months to a year or more if it loses overseas compute. CNBC (Nov 26, two unnamed people): chip sellers told neoclouds they will not supply NVIDIA chips if any capacity is rented to Chinese companies. A third report (The Information, Nov 26, in the feed via @elonmusk repost): Chinese firms are exploring handing data-centre leases to non-Chinese third parties and leasing compute back. Reports side by side, unreconciled; the rule itself is the BIS interim final rule already on the site.
why_for_agiright: First reported effects of the remote-access rule and of distillation safeguards on Chinese frontier-model timelines.
doubts: Reuters read via Yahoo republication (investing.com 403). All three are anonymous-source reports. Run 44 left out a single sell-side note on GLM-5.5 timing; this is a broader Reuters report.

author_or_publisher: PPC Land, quoting Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier (midday briefing, Nov 25)
